questions.skill: Describe how much two distributions overlap using the difference in means as a multiple of the MAD
questions.prompt: The dot plots show the heights of two kinds of plants, in centimeters. The means are 10 and 11, and each data set has a MAD of 2. Write the difference in the means as a multiple of the MAD, and describe how much the dot plots overlap.
questions.prompt_markup:
The dot plots show the heights of two kinds of plants, in centimeters. The means are 10 and 11, and each data set has a MAD of 2.
Write the difference in the means as a multiple of the MAD, and describe how much the dot plots overlap.
questions.correct_answer: 0.5 MAD; the dot plots overlap a lot (most values of each set are inside the range of the other).

figure.description: [1] Dot plot titled "Plant A (Height (cm))", number line from 4 to 16. Dots per value: 6: 1, 8: 3, 10: 2, 12: 3, 14: 1. [2] Dot plot titled "Plant B (Height (cm))", number line from 4 to 16. Dots per value: 7: 1, 9: 3, 11: 2, 13: 3, 15: 1.

questions.skill: Describe how much two distributions overlap using the difference in means as a multiple of the MAD
questions.prompt: The dot plots show the minutes two groups spent reading. The means are 10 and 14, and each data set has a MAD of 2. Which statement describes the dot plots?
questions.prompt_markup:
The dot plots show the minutes two groups spent reading. The means are 10 and 14, and each data set has a MAD of 2.
Which statement describes the dot plots?

choices.text: The means differ by 2 MADs, and the plots overlap somewhat.
The means are the same, so the plots overlap completely.
The means differ by 2 MADs, so the plots cannot share any values.
The means differ by 4 MADs, and the plots do not overlap.

questions.correct_answer: The means differ by 2 MADs, and the plots overlap somewhat.
